comparator.name: Media Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The redesigned 180 EC curriculum applies to students starting in September 2026. It combines media theory, history, analysis and production with research methods, a minor and a thesis.
components: Stories We Live By: Mediating Identities
One of two faculty-wide courses. This example uses Stories We Live By.
The alternative choice is Political Action in the Network Society.
This example uses the Global Change theme.
Complete Audiences and Uses, Analyzing Media and the selected technology or political action course before the seminar.
Choose one of the three thematic options offered.
The alternative choice is Digital Curation.
Media Careers: Prospects in the Market
Complete all 60 first-year credits and at least 50 second-year credits, including Media and Power and the Research Seminar.

alternatives.label: Media, Culture and Society
alternatives.labelReason: Media, rhetoric and sociology foundations lead into media history, representation and research. Later work applies these tools to documentary, literary adaptation and public communication.
alternatives.concept: Study how media forms shape public life and cultural identity. Combine film and media history, narrative analysis, sociology and rhetoric with research and documentary production.
progression: Media, rhetoric and sociology foundations lead into media history, representation and research. Later work applies these tools to documentary, literary adaptation and public communication.

alternatives.label: Media Industries, Communication and Audiences
alternatives.labelReason: Entrepreneurship, economics and research methods precede audience and consumer analysis, digital strategy and market research. Media courses keep the study anchored in representation, audiences and production.
alternatives.concept: Study media organisations, markets and audiences. Combine media analysis and communication practice with consumer behaviour, digital business strategy, marketing and audience research.
progression: Entrepreneurship, economics and research methods precede audience and consumer analysis, digital strategy and market research. Media courses keep the study anchored in representation, audiences and production.
alternatives.distinctness: Adds market and consumer research, behavioural economics and organisational strategy to media studies.

alternatives.label: Digital Media, Data and Responsible AI
alternatives.labelReason: Programming and mathematical methods support machine learning and neural networks. Research methods and databases support analysis, while media courses and AI ethics frame questions about representation and digital culture.
alternatives.concept: Study how digital media and algorithmic systems shape public communication. Combine media history and analysis with data management, machine learning, AI ethics and creative production.
progression: Programming and mathematical methods support machine learning and neural networks. Research methods and databases support analysis, while media courses and AI ethics frame questions about representation and digital culture.
alternatives.distinctness: Adds programming, databases and algorithmic methods to media studies, alongside ethical analysis.

selection.assessment: The broad option covers media forms, histories, audiences, representation and production. A second option adds audience markets and organisational strategy. A third emphasises digital culture and computation. All three contain sustained media study and are distinct. Journalism and political communication remain evidenced directions beyond the three-option limit.

core: Media theory, history and comparative cultural analysis
Media content, representation, audiences, use and production
Media institutions, industries, power and political-economic context
Digital platforms, networks, futures and public communication
Qualitative and quantitative research, professional practice and independent inquiry
adjacent: Cultural industries, media organisations, audiences and markets
Digital cultures, datafication and responsible artificial intelligence
Journalism, public information and media writing
questions: How do media forms and platforms shape meaning, identity and everyday life?
How do institutions, markets and political power shape media production and public information?

blocks: Media theory, history and everyday life
UCR introduces qualitative study of social meaning. Groningen teaches methods for studying media.
Both examine how narratives shape identity. UCR focuses on life and travel writing. Groningen draws on a wider range of media.
Both analyse media forms and representation. Groningen also introduces media production and audiences as research areas.
Both use historical perspectives to understand media. UCR examines the material forms and uses of older media technologies.
Groningen offers a dedicated course on media in everyday life.
Groningen focuses on media audiences and uses. UCR develops related perspectives in psychology and communication.
Media analysis, power, representation and research
Both consider changes associated with digital technologies. UCR focuses on business strategy and organisational transformation.
UCR examines how storytelling and power work across television and digital media. Groningen focuses on media networks and platforms.
Both examine media representation. UCR focuses on race, storytelling and power. Groningen also studies archives.
The Documentary brings media analysis and production together in one form. Groningen also considers use across a wider range of media.
Groningen teaches theories of media and power in a separate course.
The example uses the Global Change faculty-wide course.
Groningen requires a dedicated media research seminar after the earlier media theory and analysis courses.
Students select one of the available thematic courses.
Groningen studies specialist media thinkers and theories.
Groningen requires a separate advanced course in media research methods.
Media industries, audiences and professional practice
Groningen teaches professional writing for different media.
Groningen has a course on career prospects in the media sector.
Digital media, data and responsible AI
Groningen has a dedicated course on designing digital futures.
Open curriculum, content creation and thesis
This example uses Content Creation. At UCR, The Documentary develops production skills, and Creative Communication Laboratory focuses on experimental literary forms.
Groningen requires a media studies thesis. Independent research at UCR is optional.

notes.text: Groningen requires a sequence in media theory, research, platforms and production, plus a thesis. UCR offers related study across media, social science, business and computing. Specialist media research and professional writing have more limited coverage.
This comparison uses the redesigned curriculum for students starting in September 2026.

audience.programmeDescription: Media Studies at the University of Groningen examines media forms, production, audiences and their role in society. Students develop research skills, take a minor and write a thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines media history, representation and production. The other options give greater weight to media industries and audiences or to digital media and computing. Groningen has more dedicated media research and professional courses.
